name: Calyptosuchus
sum: Calyptosuchus is a heavily armoured aetosaur with a pig-like snout from the Late Triassic of North America.
wsnote: Estimated at about 4 m long or possibly larger, with a carapace up to almost 70 cm wide (Wikipedia).
holotype: Not stated in the sources consulted for this draft; the species was named by Long and Ballew in 1985.
material: Abundant remains, mostly osteoderms, from the Chinle, Tecovas, Santa Rosa and Petrified Forest formations; redescribed by Parker in 2018.
biology: Heavily armoured with a pig-like snout probably used to uproot plants; its dorsal and lateral osteoderms were not fully fused.
author: Long and Ballew 1985

sources.text: R. A. Long and K. L. Ballew. 1985. Aetosaur dermal armor from the Late Triassic of southwestern North America, with special reference to material from the Chinle Formation of Petrified Forest National Park. Museum of Northern Arizona Bulletin 54:45-68
